prompt: A water pump raises 120 kg of water from an underground well through a vertical height of 8.0 m every minute. The electrical power input to the pump motor is 250 W. Take g = 9.81 m s^-2. What is the efficiency of the pump?

answer.explanation: Useful work per minute = mgh = 120 * 9.81 * 8.0 = 9417.6 J. Time interval = 60 s. Useful output power = 9417.6 / 60 = 156.96 W. Efficiency = useful power / input power = 156.96 / 250 = 0.628 = 63%.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 calculates useful power using t = 1 s instead of converting minute to seconds, then dividing inappropriately.
Option 2 calculates the wasted fraction: 100% - 63% = 37% approx 38%.
Option 3 is correct: P_useful = (120 * 9.81 * 8.0) / 60 = 157 W; efficiency = 157 / 250 = 63%.
Option 4 fails to convert 1 minute into 60 seconds when calculating energy input or work.
hints: Ensure time is converted into seconds: 1 minute = 60 s.
Calculate useful power output as mgh / 60, then compare with input power 250 W.
solution: P_useful = (120 * 9.81 * 8.0) / 60 = 156.96 W. Efficiency = 156.96 / 250 = 0.628 = 63%. Option C is correct.
